### Source-verified schedule — BH775; unit applicability pending

According to the retrieved revision, for units **24898 and 24899**, pending nameplate/revision confirmation: temperature calibration and over-temperature detection checks every **6 months or 500 operating hours**, and after servicing; filter replacement every **12 months or 500 hours**. Use the specified Model 22110 fixture and calibrated thermometer. Delivered-air settings are **32, 38 and 43°C, each ±1.5°C**; this operating specification is not a substitute for the detailed service-test criteria. Record each task’s prior date and hour reading; do not automatically assign annual May PM. [Manufacturer service manual 202526A, printed pp. 8, 12–15, 19](https://assets.solventum.com/is/content/mmmspinco/Bair-Hugger-Therapy-775-Service-Manual-Englishpdf).
**Other models:** Most OEM intervals, procedures and numeric tolerances remain unverified. The MAC 1200 annual inspection recommendation is now cited in its unit record. The task prompts below are proposed review scopes, not manufacturer-approved service instructions. Do not use generic annual intervals or numeric pass limits.
### Unit-level evidence coverage

Every asset now has a compliance evidence summary, actual-history status, issue watchlist and event log. Manufacturer-authored issue summaries are included for **36 units**; **37 units** have explicit model/source verification gaps and proposed history questions. No technician-community claims have been added without a verified, attributable report. Troubleshooting lists describe possible conditions, not proof that issues are frequent. Match sources to the unit’s exact variant/software before use.

Facility applicability: confirm Ohio ASF licensing, Medicare ASC certification and accreditor. Unit-level evidence lists are TechFlex review prompts supporting C1–C4, not additional legal requirements. A missing record is an evidence gap, not a proven equipment failure. A passing PM alone does not certify facility-wide compliance.

### Evidence audit — September 15, 2026

**Audit outcome:** All 73 records have inventory provenance and conditional regulatory citations. Model-issue evidence is source-supported for 36 records; 37 remain explicitly unverified. Source verification does not establish a nameplate/software match, present compliance, failure frequency, or actual asset history.

**Reading the evidence:** S0 = supplied inventory; C1–C3 = regulatory/guidance sources; M01–M18 = manufacturer-authored documents; R1 = historical manufacturer correction notice. Each source has a locator and review status below. Third-party-hosted manufacturer manuals are identified. No unsourced community opinion is treated as evidence.

**Limits:** Retrieved manual revisions are not certified as the latest applicable revisions. Medfusion and Olympus document re-fetches failed during this audit; their previously retrieved evidence is retained with that access limitation disclosed. Midmark 224 uses an alternate indexed OEM link after a re-fetch failure. Facility accreditation, physical identifiers, software, completed PM tasks and measured results still need facility records. Proposed tasks, priorities and history questions are marked as TechFlex draft judgments, not verified facts.
